AI Appetite and Assessment Guide

Two apps support one engagement. In the appetite app the insurer settles its appetite for AI risk, for the board to approve. In the assessment app Triodian measures the AI used in the insurer’s supply chain against that appetite, and what the assessment finds also informs the appetite. This guide shows each role what to do, in which app, and when.

Appetite app

AI Risk Appetite

Records the insurer’s positions on eight decisions, tests them for consistency, and produces the appetite statement for board approval, the tolerance and trigger schedule, and the calibration set.

risk-appetite.triodian.com · sign-in required · saved as you work

Assessment app

AI Use Assessment

Maps and classifies each AI use in the arrangements assessed, tests what evidence can be obtained, and sets a finding for each arrangement. Reads the calibration set and produces the register extract the appetite app reads.

Runs in the browser · work is saved to files

Scope.Neither app gives legal advice or recommends a product. The appetite app records the positions the insurer proposes and the board approves; it does not suggest what the appetite should be. The assessment app records what documents show and how AI uses are classified; counsel determines what the law requires.

Before you start

Practise with the worked example

Both apps include a worked example: a fictional insurer, Corvane General, part-way through the engagement and labelled fictional on every screen. Use it to learn the screens before you work on the real engagement. In the appetite app, choose Practise with the worked example on the opening screen or in the menu. A short page explains what the example has already done before it opens.

Signing in and your role

Appetite app You sign in with your email address; a one-time code is sent to it. An administrator adds you as a user and gives you your engagement role, and that role decides what you can change. A control you cannot use is greyed out, and the app says why. Your name and role are recorded against every change you make. Your initials, at the top right, open your profile, where you can change your name, organisation or email address.

In practice mode you can act as any role, using Acting as in the yellow practice bar, to see what each role can and cannot change.

Assessment app There is no sign-in. Choose your name under Acting as at the right of the header. Your role then decides what you can change, and your name is recorded against every change, so check Acting as before you edit.

Where the work is kept

  • Appetite app The engagement is saved to the server as you work; a status in the header shows “Saved”. If someone else saves first, the app tells you and offers your version as a file before loading theirs. Download a copy (.json) in the menu keeps a file copy.
  • Assessment app The work stays in your browser. Save it with Save assessment (.json) and open it again with Open assessment file. Autosave to browser storage is off by default because devices may be shared.
  • Both apps underline key terms; select one for a short definition. This guide does the same, and every definition is collected under Key terms.
Privilege.The privilege marking that counsel directs is printed as the first line of every output, and the appetite app shows it under the header on every screen. Assessment files hold verbatim agreement extracts and counsel’s responses. Store and send every file as counsel directs.

On a phone

Both apps work at phone width. Grids become one card per row, and details open in a panel from the bottom of the screen.

Everyone

How the two apps fit together

The two pieces of work start in the same week and run side by side. The assessment’s first phases need no appetite, and what they find informs the appetite sessions. Once the CRO agrees a working appetite, the assessment classifies and reports against it while challenge and board approval continue.

When
Appetite app
Assessment app
Week 1
Triodian and counsel fill starting positions from the insurer’s documents, inputs I1 to I11. Session 1: decisions 1 to 3.
Phases 0 to 2: mobilise, confirm the set of arrangements, and map the AI in each. No appetite is needed for these phases.
Assessment informs appetite. The register extract is loaded on decision 3 as the evidence held today, and arrangements from the set are used to test each decision before it is recorded.
Week 2
Session 2: decisions 4 to 8. Consistency checks K1 to K10. The CRO agrees the working appetite.
Mapping continues. Classification waits for the calibration set.
Appetite calibrates assessment. The calibration set (P1 to P11), marked working, is loaded in the assessment app’s set-up.
Weeks 3 and after
Challenge from the second line and accountable persons. Counsel drafts the statement; the CRO recommends it; the board approves. The calibration set is re-issued, marked approved.
Phases 3 to 7: classify and test, questions to counsel, findings, independent check and close. A new calibration version re-runs the rules and produces a difference report.

Two files pass between the apps

Appetite app

Outputs → Calibration set → Download .json

The positions as parameters P1 to P11, with status, version, date and approver.

Calibration set →
← Register extract

The extract carries, for each entry: function, location in the supply chain, authority tier, consequence and the evidence received today. It carries no facts, sources or client wording.

Assessment app

Set-up → Load calibration set

The extract is produced from Outputs → Register extract (.json) and loaded in the appetite app on decision 3, under the current state.

Without a calibration set, the assessment app shows Uncalibrated: framework defaults apply on every screen and output. When a new version is loaded it recalculates and writes a difference report listing every result that changed. Facts, classifications and counsel’s determinations are not changed.

How the assessment informs the appetite

The appetite is meant to reflect how the insurer actually uses AI, not an abstract position. The assessment is the main evidence of that use. It can inform the appetite at five points. In each case the assessment supplies facts; the positions still come from the insurer, and counsel advises on what the insurer is obliged to do.

From the assessmentUsed in the appetiteWhat it shows the people setting the appetite
The register: the authority tier of each AI use, by function and location in the supply chainDecision 1, authorityHow much authority AI already holds, alongside the AI inventory (I7) and delegated authorities (I8), so the ceilings are set with today’s use in view. Once the appetite is set, any use above a ceiling is flagged.
The register extract: evidence received today for each combination of authority and consequenceDecision 3, evidence expectation, and check K10The current state that decision 3 starts from. Check K10 warns when the expectation for the most common combination is above anything the insurer obtains today, so the board sets that position knowing most arrangements will show a gap from the first day.
Findings: the size of each gap between required and obtainable evidenceDecision 4, shortfall toleranceHow large and how common shortfalls are, so priorities and time limits are realistic.
Facts recorded as not known, F4 findings, and confidenceDecision 5, unknownsHow much the insurer’s own documents leave unknown, and how firmly evidence is established, before limits and a minimum confidence are set.
The location and platform recorded for each entryDecision 6, location and concentrationWhich jurisdictions appear in the supply chain, which are marked on decision 6, and what share of critical operations depends on a single platform or AI model provider.

Using a real arrangement. In the sessions, each decision is tested against one of the arrangements in the assessment’s set before it is recorded. This keeps every position grounded in an arrangement the insurer actually has.

If an assessment has already been completed. Where Triodian has already completed an assessment on the framework’s defaults, its register and findings can be used in the same way: load the register extract on decision 3 and draw on the findings when setting decisions 1, 4, 5 and 6. When the CRO agrees the working appetite, load the calibration set into the assessment. The assessment re-runs its rules and lists every result that changed in the difference report; facts and counsel’s determinations are not changed.

Keep the two records apart.The register extract carries no facts, sources or client wording, so it can pass to the appetite engagement without the assessment’s working papers. The calibration set holds only positions and thresholds, so it can pass to the assessment team without the session record. Counsel decides how each is handled.

Key terms

Terms used in both apps and in this guide. Underlined terms elsewhere on the page open these definitions.

No term matches.

The engagement

AI risk appetiteAppetite
The board’s statement of how much authority AI may hold, what failures it will tolerate, and what evidence it expects the insurer to hold. It sits within the insurer’s risk appetite statement.
Risk appetite statementBoth apps
The board-approved statement of the risk the insurer is prepared to accept. The AI risk appetite sits within it.
Working appetiteAppetite
The positions the CRO has agreed, used to calibrate the assessment before the board approves them.
Calibration setBoth apps
The board's appetite as eleven parameters, P1 to P11, saved as a file from the appetite app and loaded into the assessment app. It is marked working when the CRO agrees it and approved when the board does.
Calibration statusBoth apps
Where the calibration set stands: default (no set agreed; framework defaults apply), working, or approved. Every output shows the status and version in its header.
VersionBoth apps
The number of the calibration set. It rises by one each time an agreed position changes; the approved version stays in the history.
UncalibratedAssessment
No calibration set is loaded, so the framework's defaults apply. Shown in a banner on every screen and output.
Difference reportAssessment
What changed in the assessment's results when a new calibration version was loaded, entry by entry, from what to what.
Register extractBoth apps
A file from the assessment app giving, for each entry, its function, location in the supply chain, authority tier, consequence and the evidence received today. It carries no facts, sources or client wording. The appetite app reads it as the current state for decision 3 and for check K10.
Worked exampleBoth apps
A fictional insurer loaded with sample data, labelled fictional on every screen. For learning the apps, not for client work. In the appetite app it opens in practice mode.
Privilege markingBoth apps
The marking counsel directs for the work, printed on the first line of every output.

The eleven parameters

CodeParameterSet inIf not set
P1Authority ceilingsDecision 1No above-ceiling flag is produced
P2Consequence thresholdsDecision 2The generic consequence definitions apply
P3Evidence expectationDecision 3The framework's reference table applies
P4Gap priorityDecision 4The framework's priority matrix applies
P5Time limits and interim positionsDecision 4Priority is reported without a due date
P6Not-known limitsDecision 5Not-known facts are counted and reported only
P7Minimum confidenceDecision 5Confidence is reported beside the finding
P8Location markingsDecision 6Every location is treated as "escalate"
P9Concentration limitDecision 6The share is reported without a limit
P10TriggersDecision 7The eight default triggers, without thresholds or times
P11Change events and review intervalDecision 8Reviewed annually

People and roles

Acting asBoth apps
In the assessment app, the person chosen in the header; their role decides what they can change, and their name is recorded against every change. In the appetite app it appears only in practice mode; otherwise you act as yourself, with the role an administrator gave you.
AdministratorAppetite
A user who adds and manages users and their roles, and completes set-up. Being an administrator does not by itself allow changing decisions; that needs an engagement role.
Practice modeAppetite
The worked example in the appetite app. You can act as any role, and nothing is saved.
CounselBoth apps
The legal adviser who makes every legal determination in the engagement: external counsel, or the insurer's own legal team where it holds the role.
Independent reviewerBoth apps
The party outside Triodian that checks whether the assessment is sound and its findings supported, on behalf of the CRO. In the appetite, it may advise on decision 2 only.
Reporting lineAssessment
Whether the independent reviewer reports through counsel or directly to the CRO. It decides who receives the review pack and who confirms R7.
Peer reviewerAssessment
The Triodian person who re-derives an entry's tier blind. Never the person who classified that entry.
ProposerAppetite
The person who puts a position forward. Only the CRO or the insurer's risk function may propose on decisions 1 and 3; decision 2 also admits the independent reviewer. Counsel and Triodian record positions but never propose.
Accountable personBoth apps
The senior person responsible for a function under the Financial Accountability Regime.
Arrangement ownerAssessment
The person in the insurer who owns a provider relationship, binder or claims agreement. Confirms failure consequence and accepts the hand-back list.
Separation of dutiesAssessment
The rules the app enforces by person: the peer reviewer did not classify the entry; the validator classified and reviewed nothing in the set; the annex signer is not the only peer reviewer of any entry.

The appetite

DecisionAppetite
One of eight questions settled in the sessions and approved by the board, each recorded with a proposer and an owner. Decisions 1 to 3 are taken in session 1; 4 to 8 in session 2.
Starting positionAppetite
A value filled in from the insurer’s own documents as a basis for discussion. It is not a recommendation and is never filled in automatically.
Current stateAppetite
What the insurer has or holds today. The starting point for decisions 1 and 3.
Reference tableAppetite
The framework's default evidence expectations (appendix A). Shown on decision 3 only if the insurer asks, and the session record notes that it was shown.
Not setAppetite
A position deliberately left open, with an owner and a due date. A not-set item falls back to the framework default in the calibration set.
CeilingBoth apps
The highest authority tier the board accepts for a function and location in the chain (P1).
ConditionAppetite
A limit attached to a ceiling, such as a maximum amount. It must be capable of being checked against documents.
Critical operationBoth apps
A business process whose disruption the insurer has assessed as critical, with a tolerance set by the board.
Tolerance levelAppetite
The maximum disruption the board accepts for a critical operation.
TriggerBoth apps
A defined event that must be reported to the insurer within a set time (P10).
Consistency checkAppetite
One of ten tests, K1 to K10, run on the recorded positions. K1 to K9 must pass before the working appetite can be agreed; K10 is a warning.
ChallengeAppetite
A point raised by the second line or an accountable person against an agreed position, recorded as open, accepted or answered.

The assessment

ArrangementAssessment
One relationship assessed: a provider, the platform behind it, or an external AI service the insurer's staff use.
Representative setAssessment
The arrangements the GC and counsel agree to assess, chosen against six criteria. Not the whole estate.
BoundaryBoth apps
Where evidence must cross between parties: B1 insurer to provider, B2 provider to the platform behind it, B3 the insurer's own use.
Material service providerBoth apps
A provider the insurer relies on for a critical operation or to manage a material risk.
Platform behind a providerBoth apps
The technology, pricing or AI model a provider relies on: the fourth party.
Register entryAssessment
One place AI acts within an arrangement, recorded in 26 fields.
Seven questionsAssessment
The ordered questions put to every arrangement, from whether CPS 230 reaches the party to what evidence can reasonably be required. Counsel determines questions 1 to 4 and 7.
Source referenceAssessment
The document and page, or interview and date, behind a value, for example D5-ARR02 p.14.
Not knownBoth apps
A fact the documents do not show. Such facts are counted, not estimated.
Question to counselAssessment
A numbered written question for a legal determination. It is not answered in a working paper.
TranscribedAssessment
Counsel's response entered verbatim by a Triodian person, with the question reference recorded.
Phase gateAssessment
The conditions that close each of the eight phases. Work can run ahead of a gate, but outputs produced before it is met are marked draft.
Draft and finalAssessment
Every output is marked draft until its phase gate is met and the legal-line check is cleared; only then can it be exported as final.

The scales and the ladder

Authority tierBoth apps
How much an AI can do on its own, from A1 productivity (a person still acts) to A6 actuation (it holds credentials that change systems).
Consequence levelBoth apps
How serious a failure would be, from C1 immaterial to C5 critical-operation disruption, set against the insurer's own thresholds (P2).
Evidence rungBoth apps
A type of evidence about an AI's behaviour, from E0 none to E6 deterministic actuation control.
Evidence ladderBoth apps
The seven evidence rungs in order of strength.
Indicative rungAssessment
The framework's default rung for a tier and consequence, used when no calibration set is loaded.
Expected rungBoth apps
The evidence the board expects for a tier and consequence, read from the calibration set (P3).
Required rungBoth apps
The evidence the insurer can reasonably require at a boundary, as determined with counsel.
Obtainable rungBoth apps
The highest rung at which all five obtainability tests pass: the evidence that can in fact be produced and independently checked.
Obtainability testAssessment
Five conditions tested at each rung: T1 produced, T2 aggregate, T3 reachable, T4 checkable, T5 timely. A failure steps down one rung.
ConfidenceBoth apps
How firmly an obtainable rung is established: high if the record has been seen, medium if a document describes it, low if inferred.

Rung and test codes

CodeMeaning
E0None. No evidence is held.
E1Disclosure: a statement of what AI is used, where and for what.
E2Attestation: a signed statement that the AI operated within stated limits over a period.
E3Event notification: notice when a defined trigger is crossed.
E4Audit: a right to examine the aggregate record.
E5Continuous telemetry: a stream of aggregate measures against the declared appetite.
E6Deterministic actuation control: a control at the point of action, independent of the AI's reasoning, with a signed record of what was requested and allowed.
T1Produced: a record of this type exists, or could be generated without redesign.
T2Aggregate: it can be given without individual decisions, policyholder data or the model.
T3Reachable: a term in force, or a contracting point, lets the record reach the insurer.
T4Checkable: someone independent of the producer can verify it.
T5Timely: it arrives in time for the insurer to act and meet its own notification obligations.

Findings and flags

FindingAssessment
The result for one arrangement: F1, F2, F3 or F4. Shown as "awaiting counsel" until counsel has set the required rung.
F1 Evidence obtainableAssessment
The obtainable rung meets the required rung.
F2 GapAssessment
The obtainable rung falls short of the required rung.
F3 No reasonable reachAssessment
Counsel has determined the insurer cannot reasonably require evidence here. A documented conclusion, not a gap.
F4 Not determinableBoth apps
The documents cannot show whether, or how, AI is used.
GapBoth apps
The number of rungs between the required and the obtainable rung. Used only where counsel has set a required rung.
Gap priorityBoth apps
How serious a gap is, from its size and the consequence level (P4).
Interim positionBoth apps
What the insurer does while a gap stands: restrict, compensate or accept (P5).
FlagAssessment
A signal reported beside a finding, never inside it: above ceiling, location, below minimum confidence, not known over limit, F4 standing too long, or concentration.
Above ceilingBoth apps
An AI use whose authority is higher than the ceiling the board set (P1).
ConcentrationBoth apps
The share of critical operations in the set that depend on one platform or model provider, measured against the board's limit (P9).

Review and outputs

Review pointAssessment
One of seven checks, R1 to R7, each with a reviewer, a date and a result.
Blind re-derivationAssessment
Review point R3: the peer reviewer sets an entry's tier from the facts alone, without seeing the first classification.
Legal-line checkAssessment
Review point R5: a scan of drafts for wording that states what the law requires. Every hit is changed or cleared before final export.
Independent checkAssessment
Review point R7: the independent reviewer's review, complete when every point they raise is closed or disclosed.
Exceptions logAssessment
A record of each departure from the method, with its reason, who approved it and when.
Review packAssessment
The register, evidence worksheets, technical annex and exceptions log, addressed to whoever the reporting line names.
Technical scheduleAssessment
The evidence items, tolerances and triggers for each F1 and F2, written to sit beside counsel's flow-down clauses (DL4).
Technical annexAssessment
Triodian's report of the assessment, in its own name (DL5).
Hand-back listAssessment
AI uses found that are not on the insurer's inventory, returned to the inventory owner (DL6).

Role

Board

Appetite app

You approve, amend or return the AI risk appetite on the CRO’s recommendation. Counsel drafts the statement in a form you can approve. Once approved, the calibration set is marked approved and becomes what the assessment measures against.

Appetite

Record the approval

  1. Sign in. The board secretariat or company secretary holds the Board record role.
  2. Go to Outputs. Read the Statement and the Schedule. Each shows the status, version and date in its header.
  3. After the meeting, under Record board approval, enter the date, the minute reference and the board or committee that approved it. This is available once the CRO has agreed a working appetite.
Not available to this role:Edit positions. The board record role changes the approval fields only.
  • Any later change to a position returns the set to working and raises the version. The approved version stays in the history.
  • If the independent reviewer advised on the consequence thresholds, the statement says so. The same reviewer later reviews findings measured against those thresholds.
Back to roles
Role

CRO

Appetite appAssessment app

You and the insurer risk function propose the appetite, and you agree the working appetite. In the assessment, the independent reviewer reviews the work on your behalf.

Appetite

Propose and agree the appetite

  1. Start at Decisions. Each card shows the decision's status, its session and open questions for counsel.
  1. On each decision, read the starting position: what the insurer's documents already say. Use starting position copies it into empty cells; nothing is copied automatically. Decision 3 starts from the current state: the evidence the insurer holds today.
  2. Propose positions. Only you or the risk function can be named as proposer on decisions 1 and 3. Counsel and Triodian may record a position on your behalf, and the record shows both. Each position’s proposer, owner, condition and any dissent are under Details in its cell.
  3. Any cell can be recorded as not set, with an owner and a due date.
  1. Open Checks. K1 to K9 must pass before the working appetite can be agreed. Each failure links to the position concerned and opens its details. K10 is a warning, not a failure.
  1. On Outputs, select Agree working appetite. Only the CRO can do this, signed in as themselves. The calibration set becomes working, version 1.
  2. Respond to points in Challenge. You or counsel write the overall-position paragraph of the statement, and you recommend the statement to the board.
Not available to this role:Approve on behalf of the board.
Assessment

Receive the independent review

You are chosen at set-up as the CRO, and the independent reviewer's reporting line is set to one of two options.

  • Directly to the CRO: the review pack is addressed to you, and you confirm review point R7 on the Review screen once every review point is closed or disclosed.
  • Through counsel: counsel receives the pack, and the independent reviewer confirms R7.

Role

Insurer risk function

Appetite app

As the second line, you propose positions with the CRO and challenge them once agreed.

Appetite

Propose, then challenge

  1. Start at Decisions and work through each decision as the CRO does. You may propose on every decision.
  2. Once the working appetite is agreed, open Challenge. Log each point with the decision and cell it concerns. Filter by accountable person to see each area's points.
  3. You, the CRO and counsel record responses. A point is open, accepted or answered. An accepted point links to the position it changed.
Not available to this role:Agree the working appetite. That is the CRO's.

Role

General counsel

Assessment app

You confirm the scope of the assessment and agree which arrangements it covers. In the appetite engagement you attend session 1 but hold no role in the app.

Assessment

Confirm the brief and agree the set

  1. Set-up: confirm the brief with a date and reference. This is part of the phase 0 gate.
  2. Set: review the arrangements selected (ARR-01 onward), the criteria each meets and the coverage strip. The strip shows whether the three boundary types are represented: B1 insurer to provider, B2 provider to the platform behind it, and B3 the insurer's own use.
  3. Record your agreement. Counsel records theirs separately. Together they are review point R1 and the phase 1 gate.
Not available to this role:Edit the register.
Back to roles
Role

Arrangement owner

Assessment app

You own an arrangement in the insurer: a provider relationship, a binder or a claims agreement. You confirm what failure could do, and you accept the AI uses found that are not on the insurer's inventory.

Assessment

Confirm consequence, accept the hand-back

  1. Classify and test → 2 · Consequence: check the level proposed for each entry in your arrangement against the insurer's thresholds, C1 to C5. Select Confirm as arrangement owner.
  1. Outputs → DL6 Hand-back list: review the AI uses found that are not on the inventory, and select Accept hand-back list. This closes phase 7.
Not available to this role:Edit classifications.
Back to roles
Role

Counsel

Appetite appAssessment app

You facilitate the appetite sessions and settle the statement. In the assessment you determine the legal questions: whether CPS 230 reaches each arrangement, what rights the insurer holds, and what evidence it can require. Triodian works for you on technical matters.

Appetite

Facilitate and settle

  1. Lead the sessions from Decisions, one decision at a time and in order. Session 1 covers decisions 1 to 3; session 2 covers decisions 4 to 8. Positions come from the insurer; you explain and answer questions but do not propose.
  2. Record each position with its proposer, condition and any dissent. Park questions for counsel as they arise; they collect in one shared list.
  3. On decision 3, load the assessment register extract if one is available; it fills the current state. The reference table is behind Show reference table. Show it only if the insurer asks; the session record notes when it was shown.
  4. After challenge, settle the statement and schedule in Outputs, in a form the board can approve. You or the CRO write the overall-position paragraph.
Assessment

Answer and determine

  1. Set: record your agreement to the set (R1), alongside the GC's.
  2. Counsel: answer each question in the log. Each states which of the seven questions it relates to, the facts with sources, why it matters, and the question itself. You determine questions 1 to 4 and 7, and the authority delegated under question 5.
  3. Enter determinations into fields 23 to 25 of each entry, from the answered question. You may enter them yourself, or Triodian may transcribe your response verbatim; the record shows who transcribed it. Only the newest answer for an entry can be applied. To change a determination, answer a new question.
  4. Review: record your review of the drafts (R6). Drafts reach you before anyone else.
  5. If the independent reviewer reports through counsel, the review pack is addressed to you.

How findings follow your answers. Where your answers to questions 1 to 3 are no nexus, no relationship and passive rights only, or you record that there is no reasonable reach, the arrangement's finding is F3. Until you set the required rung, the arrangement shows as awaiting counsel.

Not available to this role:Be named as proposer on any appetite decision. Edit facts, classifications or test results in the assessment.
Back to roles
Role

Independent reviewer

Appetite appAssessment app

You review the assessment on behalf of the CRO: is it sound, and are its findings supported? You also advise on the consequence thresholds in the appetite. The apps show your role, never your firm.

Appetite

Advise on decision 2

  1. Open Decision 2 · Consequence thresholds. Propose and comment on the thresholds for C1 to C5, including one for each critical operation, and raise questions and challenge on decision 2.
  2. The statement discloses that you advised on these thresholds and will later review findings measured against them.
Assessment

Review on behalf of the CRO

  1. Open Outputs → RP Review pack. It holds the register (DL1), the evidence worksheets (DL2), the technical annex (DL5) and the exceptions log, addressed by the reporting line.
  1. On Review → Independent review points, log each point with the output and section it concerns. Triodian responds.
  2. Close or disclose each point. Only you can.
  3. When every point is closed or disclosed, R7 can be confirmed: by you when the line is through counsel, by the CRO when it runs directly to the CRO.
Not available to this role:Edit any appetite decision other than decision 2. Edit anything in the assessment other than review points.
Back to roles
Role

Triodian

Appetite appAssessment app

In the appetite engagement you prepare the starting positions, record what is decided and run the checks. In the assessment you build and test the register and write the technical findings for counsel. You never propose an appetite position, and you never state what the law requires.

Appetite

Recorder

  1. Before session 1, check with the administrator that set-up is complete: people and roles, functions, critical operations, and inputs I1 to I11 marked as received, not held or not requested. Starting positions use the inputs marked as received.
  2. During sessions, record positions on the proposer’s behalf. Open Details in the cell and choose who you are recording for.
  3. Review Checks after each session and refer conflicts to the CRO. The checks run after every change.
  4. Once the CRO agrees, issue the calibration set from Outputs → Calibration set to the assessment team. Re-issue it on every new version.
Assessment

Five assessment roles

One person may hold several roles, but these separations are enforced by person.

RoleYou doYou cannot
Method ownerAnything Triodian can; run the legal-line check (R5); sign the technical annexEnter counsel's determinations except by transcription
AssessorBuild the register; classify; run the obtainability test; draft questions and findingsPeer-review an entry you classified
Peer reviewerRe-derive tiers blind (R3); resolve differencesReview an entry you classified
ValidationRun R4; record exceptionsEdit classifications; validate a set you classified or reviewed in
Delivery managerPeople, documents and interviews; completeness check (R2); exceptions logClassify

Delivery manager

  1. Set-up: add people and their roles. Set the independent reviewer and the reporting line. Load the calibration set.
  2. Track documents D1 to D10 and interviews. Give each received document an ID used in every source reference, such as D5-ARR02 p.14, and set its reference (D1 to D9) so the app knows which documents can support high confidence.
  3. Confirm R2: fields 1 to 14 are complete or marked not known for every entry, and every value is sourced and dated.
  4. Keep the exceptions log on Review.

Assessor

  1. Register: add an entry for each place AI acts, under its arrangement.
  1. Fill fields 1 to 14, each with a source or marked not known. Field 11 must be saved before a tier can be set.
  1. Classify and test, one entry at a time. For authority, answer the three deciding tests with sources. The app proposes a tier from A1 to A6; accept it or override it with a reason.
  1. Propose a consequence level for the arrangement owner to confirm. The expected rung is read from the calibration set, or from the base rule when uncalibrated.
  2. Run the obtainability test from the expected rung. Test T1 to T5, each with a source; a failure steps down one rung, and the obtainable rung is the first where all five pass. For A1 entries at C1, test only whether a disclosure exists.
  3. The app proposes confidence from the sources. Lowering it is free; raising it needs a reason.
  1. Counsel: raise a question from any field with Ask counsel; the reference, entry and facts are pre-filled.
  2. Findings: review each arrangement's worksheet, parts A to J. The app sets the finding type; you complete the routes and owner for any gap.

Peer reviewer

  1. Choose yourself under Acting as and open an entry you did not classify.
  2. You see fields 11 to 13 only. The classifier's tier, the rungs and the finding stay hidden on every screen until you record your tier.
  3. Set the tier. If it differs from the classifier's, both are kept side by side and a written resolution is needed. Unresolved differences block the phase 3 gate.

Validation

  1. On Review, run R4. Check that the rules for expected rungs and obtainability were applied the same way across entries, that every adjustment has a reason, and that every obtainable rung has five test results.
  2. Record any departure in the exceptions log.
  3. The app blocks R4 for anyone who classified or peer-reviewed an entry in the set.

Method owner

  1. Write the open sections of the technical annex in Outputs → DL5.
  2. Run the legal-line check (R5) on Review. It lists each phrase that states what the law requires, such as "must comply" or "breach of", with the field it came from and every output it appears in. Change the text or clear the hit; editing the text reopens it.
  3. Export final is available only when R5 is cleared and the phase 5 gate is met. Until then every output is marked Draft.
  4. Sign the annex. You cannot sign if you are the only peer reviewer of any entry.

Role

Administrator

Appetite app

You manage who can use the appetite app and complete set-up. You may also hold an engagement role; being an administrator does not by itself allow changing decisions.

Appetite

Users and set-up

  1. Open Admin from the menu. Under Users, add each person with their email address, name, organisation and engagement role. Tick Administrator for anyone else who manages users.
  2. People who sign in before they are added are listed under Waiting for access, with a button to add them.
  3. Under Set-up, start the engagement and record the engagement details, the privilege marking counsel directs, each person’s accountability areas, the functions in scope, the critical operations with their approved tolerance levels, and the status of inputs I1 to I11.
  4. Deactivate users rather than delete them, so their names stay on the positions they recorded. Activity lists user changes and engagement saves.
Not available to this role:Removing your own administrator access, or leaving the app with no active administrator.

Assessment phases and review points

The app does not stop anyone working ahead of a gate. It marks every output produced before the gate is met as draft.

Scales

ScaleCodes
AuthorityA1 productivity · A2 analytical · A3 decision · A4 transactional · A5 agentic · A6 actuation
ConsequenceC1 to C5, set against the insurer's own thresholds in decision 2
EvidenceE0 none · E1 disclosure · E2 attestation · E3 event notification · E4 audit · E5 continuous telemetry · E6 deterministic actuation control
ObtainabilityT1 to T5: produced, aggregate, reachable, checkable, timely. All five must pass at a rung

Findings and flags

FindingMeaning
F1The evidence obtainable meets the required rung
F2The evidence obtainable falls short. The worksheet gives the gap size, priority, failed test, owner and routes
F3Counsel has determined there is no reasonable reach
F4Documents do not show whether AI is used, or what it can do

Flags are reported beside findings, never as part of them. They show where an entry is above the board's authority ceiling, in a location the board has marked, below the minimum confidence, over the limit for unknowns, F4 for longer than allowed, or part of a concentration on one platform or provider.

Outputs

AppOutputs
AppetiteAI risk appetite statement · tolerance and trigger schedule · session record · calibration set · check report
AssessmentDL1 register (Markdown and CSV) · DL2 evidence worksheets · DL3 control-library shape · DL4 technical schedule · DL5 technical annex · DL6 hand-back list · QS question set · RP review pack · CM closing measures · DR difference report

Every output can be copied as Markdown or downloaded. Where a browser blocks downloads, use Copy. Each output carries the privilege marking on its first line, and its status, version and date in its header.
